title: Relative final last apex fills a join boundary
statement: Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and ordered joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $p:C\to D$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories, let $K$ be a small simplicial set and let $r>0$. Let $a:K\star\partial\Delta^r\to C$ and $b:K\star\Delta^r\to D$ satisfy $pa=b|_{K\star\partial\Delta^r}$. Suppose the already specified last apex $a(r)$ is $p$-final: for every $z\in C$ the induced map $\operatorname{Map}_C(z,a(r))\to\operatorname{Map}_D(pz,pa(r))$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, in the sense of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary]. Then there is $h:K\star\Delta^r\to C$ with $h|_{K\star\partial\Delta^r}=a$ and $ph=b$ exactly. The assertion includes $K=\varnothing$. No dimension-zero lifting or other relative limits are assumed.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (2), printed pp.337-338: last-apex relative-final boundary lifting, with its simplex-by-simplex join expansion; this is the last-apex part of the returned parent step 2. September 18, 2017 edition read online; shared archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Put $A=K\star\partial\Delta^r$ and $B=K\star\Delta^r$. The inclusion $A\hookrightarrow B$ is degreewise injective by the join definition. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to obtain a relative skeletal filtration of $B$ starting at $A$ and attaching coproducts of boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, one for each nondegenerate simplex of $B$ outside $A$. We construct the desired lift along this filtration, retaining the already specified map on every previous stage.

source.place: Proposition 1.5.5.14, proof of (b), relative skeletal filtration.

proof.text: Every nondegenerate simplex of $B$ outside $A$ has a nonempty $\Delta^r$-block equal to the full nondegenerate $r$-simplex: if the $\Delta^r$-block were a proper face, the simplex would lie in $K\star\partial\Delta^r$. Thus it is the join of a nondegenerate $d$-simplex of $K$ with $\Delta^r$, hence has dimension $n=d+r+1>0$, and its final vertex is the last vertex of the prescribed map $a$ (namely $a(r)$). This also covers $K=\varnothing$, where the only new cell is $\Delta^r$ itself.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (2), printed pp.337-338, simplex-by-simplex join expansion.

proof.text: Suppose a stage of the filtration has already been lifted over $b$. For each newly attached $n$-simplex, its attaching boundary already has a map to $C$, and its composite with $p$ is the restriction of the corresponding $n$-simplex of $b$. By step 2 its final vertex is $a(r)$ and $n>0$. The $p$-final boundary criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] therefore supplies a filler $\Delta^n\to C$ whose restriction is exactly the prescribed boundary and whose composite with $p$ is exactly the base simplex. Since the cells at a stage meet only along their attaching boundaries, choose these fillers simultaneously and obtain the next-stage lift, fixed on the preceding stage.

source.place: Corollary 7.1.5.17, final-vertex boundary-filling criterion (opposite dual), expanded simplex-by-simplex.

proof.text: At limit stages take the union of the compatible lifts. The filtration has colimit $B$, so the union is a simplicial map $h:B\to C$; every finite simplex lies in a stage, hence all face and degeneracy equations hold. Each stage was over the fixed map $b$ and agreed with $a$ on $A$, so $ph=b$ exactly and $h|_A=a$ exactly. This proves the assertion, with no dimension-zero lifting requirement because $r>0$ ensures every newly attached cell has positive dimension.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (2), printed pp.337-338, compatible union conclusion.
